All-Out Attacker.description:
Mega Raichu Y is one of the best special attackers in the tier thanks to its incredible Special Attack and Speed stats, combination of No Guard and Zap Cannon, and wide selection coverage options. Zap Cannon can 2HKO many common threats like Mega Floette, Clefable, Aegislash, and Rotom-Wash; additionally, Dragapult, which otherwise outspeeds and threatens to either KO or pivot out with U-turn, is unable to switch in due to Zap Cannon's power and guaranteed paralysis. Focus Blast provides Mega Raichu Y a way to tear through Electric-resistant and -immune foes like Archaludon and Excadrill, as well as Kingambit. Grass Knot targets Hippowdon, notably 2HKOing mixed variants, and Mega Swampert, but Alluring Voice can be ran instead, as this allows it to hit Dragapult and Garchomp for super effective damage. Surf 2HKOes specially defensive Gliscor, which otherwise walls Mega Raichu Y's Electric-type attacks. Volt Switch provides its team momentum while escaping bad matchups, such as those against Mega Dragalge, Mega Meganium, and Galarian Slowking. Substitute is another option to ease prediction around Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott trying to revenge kill it with STAB Sucker Punch while making use of the switches Mega Raichu Y forces, allowing it to spread paralysis with Zap Cannon much more easily.

Mega Raichu Y can be found on offense and bulky offense teams that benefit from its paralysis support via Zap Cannon. It also serves as an amazing speed control option for these types of teams, outpacing almost the entire unboosted metagame and pressuring it with its coverage attacks. Pokemon like Excadrill and Garchomp can pressure its checks like Mega Dragalge and Galarian Slowking with Earthquake. In return, Mega Raichu Y can threaten Corviknight and Rotom-Wash for said Ground-types. Mega Raichu Y is extremely frail, which leaves it vulnerable to faster revenge killers like Mega Lopunny and Choice Scarf users like Meowscarada, as well as causing it to struggle to switch in safely. To fix this problem, you can pair it with pivots, such as Corviknight and Galarian Slowking Corviknight's great physical bulk allows it to easily switch in on both Meowscarada and Mega Lopunny, and it can easily remove entry hazards with Defog, which can otherwise wear down Mega Raichu Y. Galarian Slowking can bring Mega Raichu Y in safely with Chilly Reception and absorb Toxic Spikes, which can otherwise wear Mega Raichu Y down. It can also provide Future Sight support to help Mega Raichu Y break through Mega Dragalge, a Pokemon that otherwise shrugs off its attacks, while making pivoting into Mega Raichu Y much more of a chore. Hisuian Samurott, in particular, is a great teammate, setting up Spikes with Ceaseless Edge while threatening faster threats to Mega Raichu Y, like Mega Delphox, with STAB Sucker Punch; a single layer of Spikes guarantees that Mega Raichu Y's Grass Knot OHKOes physically defensive variants of Hippowdon. Dark-type attackers like Kingambit, Hydreigon, and Hisuian Samurott appreciate Volt Switch support and take care of Galarian Slowking, which otherwise switches in on Mega Raichu Y, while Mega Raichu Y deals with Corviknight, Clefable, and Primarina for them.

Utility.description:
Mega Clefable is an excellent utility Pokemon that uses Magic Bounce to deter entry hazards and status moves while either making progress with Calm Mind or providing Stealth Rock support. Its Ground immunity lets it comfortably switch into and stifle common entry hazard setters such as Garchomp and Hippowdon with Magic Bounce. Magic Bounce also allows Mega Clefable to punish other status move users such as Dragapult and opposing utility Clefable. It can capitalize on these favorable matchups to begin setting up Calm Mind. It is a particularly dangerous Calm Mind sweeper, as it is immune to common anti-setup moves such as Whirlwind, Toxic, and Dragon Tail, courtesy of Magic Bounce and its Fairy typing. Alternatively, Mega Clefable can forgo its ability to become a wincon using Calm Mind and instead provide its team role compression with Stealth Rock support while also pressuring its switch-ins such as Mega Delphox. Flamethrower prevents Steel-types such as Corviknight, Aegislash, and Excadrill from freely switching in. 13 Speed SPs allow Clefable to outspeed Adamant maximum Speed Kingambit and hit it hard with either Flamethrower or Moonblast. 21 HP SPs improve Clefable's overall bulk, notably allowing it to survive Jolly Mega Lopunny's Triple Axel and Excadrill's Iron Head from full health.

Mega Clefable can be run on a variety of teamstyles, from stall to offense, thanks to its valuable utility against entry hazard setters. Sweepers such as Volcarona, Dragonite, and Ceruledge appreciate Mega Clefable's ability to keep Stealth Rock off the field, making them significantly harder to wear down or revenge kill. Volcarona and Ceruledge can pressure Steel-types such as Corviknight and Mega Mawile, while Dragonite can assist against opposing Fire-types such as Ceruledge and Blaziken. On balance and stall teams, Pokemon such as Skeledirge and Toxapex similarly appreciate Stealth Rock and Spikes being denied, to not be worn down. Mega Clefable's ability to handle Garchomp is equally valuable, while Skeledirge and Toxapex can switch into super effective Steel-, Poison-, and Ice-type coverage aimed at Mega Clefable from threats such as Scizor, Sneasler, and Meowscarada. Offensive pivots such as Meowscarada and Dragapult also enjoy Mega Clefable's hazard control, allowing them to pivot in and out of battle while safely bringing Mega Clefable in against threats such as Annihilape and Mega Meganium that may attempt to switch into specific coverage moves. Despite its utility, Mega Clefable cannot reliably stop every entry hazard setter, with setters such as Mold Breaker Excadrill, Hisuian Samurott, and Glimmora either bypassing it or threatening it out. Because of this, it pairs well with secondary entry hazard removers, such as Excadrill, Glimmora, and Quaquaval on offensive teams and Corviknight on balance teams, to ensure entry hazards remain off the field. Mega Clefable also struggles against several opposing Mega Evolutions, including Mega Delphox, Mega Metagross, and Mega Raichu Y, as well as various powerful attackers such as Sneasler, Meowscarada, and Hisuian Arcanine. It also struggles breaking past the various Poison-types with Regenerator such as Toxapex, Mega Dragalge, and Galarian Slowking. Ground-types such as Garchomp and Hippowdon pair well with Mega Clefable by setting up entry hazards to wear these Pokemon down and switching into Mega Raichu Y's Electric-type attacks while also checking Sneasler, Hisuian Arcanine, and Glimmora. They can also pressure many of Mega Clefable's usual checks, such as Toxapex, Galarian Slowking, Mega Metagross, and Skeledirge with Earthquake, paving the way for Mega Clefable to sweep with Calm Mind. Aegislash can switch into Toxapex and Galarian Slowking as well as threaten them with its powerful Shadow Ball or Poltergeist. Aegislash also matches up well against Mega Metagross, threatening it with Ghost-type STAB moves, while using Shadow Sneak to revenge kill weakened Mega Delphox. Choice Scarf users such as Hisuian Samurott and Hydreigon can also revenge kill Mega Delphox and Mega Metagross, making them valuable partners.

Dragon Dance.description:
Dragon Dance Dragonite is a threatening late-game setup sweeper, as Multiscale and its useful defensive typing naturally create setup opportunities against offensive Pokemon such as Ceruledge and Volcarona, as well as Choice-locked Meowscarada and Hisuian Samurott. Earthquake threatens Aegislash, Kingambit, Galarian Slowking, and Toxapex, while Fire Punch lets Dragonite directly pressure Skarmory, Corviknight, and Mega Scizor. Ice Spinner targets Garchomp, Dragapult, and Mega Meganium. Dragon Claw provides a reliable Dragon-type STAB attack against Pokemon such as Hydreigon and Mega Charizard X, whereas Outrage offers significantly greater power at the cost of locking Dragonite into the move and allowing Fairy-types such as Mega Floette and Clefable to switch in freely. Extreme Speed lets Dragonite clean weakened offensive teams and pick off faster foes such as Mega Lopunny and Sneasler, whereas Roost restores Dragonite's Multiscale and lets it repeatedly set up against Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott locked into Razor Shell. Leftovers best supports Roost sets by improving Dragonite's longevity, while Lum Berry lets it exploit status attempts from Pokemon such as Dragapult, Galarian Slowking, and Toxapex; notably, Jolly Dragonite can shrug off Dragapult's Will-O-Wisp or Thunder Wave, then outspeed and OHKO it with Ice Spinner after Dragon Dance. Lum Berry can also cure the confusion caused by Outrage once. Silk Scarf is best paired with an Adamant nature, significantly improving Extreme Speed's rolls against faster offensive threats; notably, after Stealth Rock, +1 Extreme Speed OHKOes Greninja and has a favourable chance to OHKO Sneasler and Meowscarada. After a Dragon Dance, Jolly Dragonite outspeeds Dragapult, Mega Raichu Y, Mega Greninja, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Delphox, while Adamant sacrifices these Speed benchmarks for greater power but still lets Dragonite outspeed Meowscarada, Greninja, Mega Metagross and Sneasler. Adamant also guarantees an OHKO on Galarian Slowking with Earthquake and has a 75% chance to OHKO opposing Dragonite through Multiscale with Ice Spinner, compared to Jolly Dragonite's 25% chance, reducing the risk of being revenge killed by Extreme Speed afterward.

Dragonite fits best on offensive teams that can keep entry hazards on the opposing side while preserving Multiscale on its own. Hisuian Samurott is one of its best partners, setting Spikes with Ceaseless Edge and switching into Ice-type attacks aimed at Dragonite. Garchomp can set Stealth Rock alongside it, further wearing down Dragonite's defensive answers, bringing faster threats into range of Extreme Speed, and breaking potential Focus Sashes on Pokemon such as Ceruledge and Glimmora. Skarmory and Corviknight wall Dragonite's coverage if it forgoes Fire Punch, making Mega Delphox a valuable partner, since it threatens both with its Fire-type attacks and discourages Corviknight from using Defog. Mega Delphox can also switch into Fairy-type attacks from Mega Floette and Clefable. Mega Clefable is another useful partner, using Magic Bounce to block entry hazards that would break Multiscale while pressuring Skarmory and Corviknight with Flamethrower. However, Magic Bounce cannot remove hazards already on the field, so Dragonite still appreciates removal from Excadrill and Corviknight. Mold Breaker Excadrill also pressures Rotom-Wash with Earthquake, though Choice Scarf variants can outspeed and force it out. Both removal options help against Fairy-types such as Mega Floette, with Corviknight additionally checking Choice Scarf Meowscarada, which outspeeds even +2 Adamant Dragonite and threatens it with Triple Axel. Galarian Slowking provides a sturdier answer to Primarina and can bring Dragonite in safely with Chilly Reception. Kingambit is another useful Fairy-type answer that can pressure Dragapult, one of the main Pokemon preventing Dragonite from freely cleaning with Extreme Speed. It is especially valuable alongside Outrage variants, as Fairy-types can switch into the move freely once Dragonite is locked in.

Bulky Attacker.description:
With high Special Attack, good natural bulk, and a fantastic ability in Mega Sol, Mega Meganium functions as a potent bulky attacker and balance breaker. Mega Sol further boosts Mega Meganium, with strong attacks like Solar Beam and reliable recovery with Synthesis ensuring that it is a consistent check to Water- and Ground-types like Primarina, Rotom-Wash, Mega Swampert, and Hippowdon. Weather Ball threatens Steel-types such as Corviknight, Aegislash, and Kingambit while also doing sizable damage to Galarian Slowking. Dazzling Gleam enables Mega Meganium to threaten Dragon-types that resist Weather Ball and Solar Beam, such as Dragonite and Hydreigon. Earth Power can be used instead to threaten potential switch-ins like Galarian Slowking, Skeledirge, and Mega Dragalge at the expense of no longer doing significant damage to the aforementioned Dragon-types. Mega Meganium should run 13 Speed SPs to outspeed Jolly Kingambit and Adamant Aegislash. 21 HP SPs allow Mega Meganium to survive an Iron Head from Excadrill, a Brave Bird from Corviknight, and a +1 Ice Spinner from Dragonite.

Mega Meganium functions best on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its offensive and defensive capabilities. It is a good teammate to sweepers like Dragon Dance Dragonite and Swords Dance Garchomp due to how it can threaten Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, which often give these Pokemon trouble. Ghost-types like Aegislash and Dragapult also appreciate its ability to switch into Dark-type attacks from Hisuian Samurott, Kingambit, and Hydreigon. Mega Meganium appreciates strong Ground-types, such as Garchomp and Excadrill, to threaten the Poison- and Fire-types that can wall sets lacking Earth Power, such as Galarian Slowking, Mega Dragalge, and Ceruledge. In return, Mega Meganium directly threatens the Water- and Grass-types that can give these Pokemon trouble, like Primarina, Rotom-Wash, and Meowscarada. It also appreciates entry hazard setters such as Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott to apply pressure to its switch-ins like Galarian Slowking and Toxapex. Hisuian Samurott in particular is a fantastic teammate thanks to its great type synergy and its ability to bring Mega Meganium in on physically bulky Pokemon, such as Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, with Flip Turn. Corviknight also makes a good partner, as it can easily switch into Poison-type moves while also switching into Triple Axel from Mega Lopunny and Meowscarada as well as Meteor Mash from Mega Metagross, which typically force Mega Meganium out. In return, Mega Meganium can reliably switch into attacks from Mega Raichu Y and Rotom-Wash. Bulky Water-types such as Primarina, Toxapex, and Rotom-Wash that can switch into the Fire-types that threaten Mega Meganium, like Blaziken, Ceruledge, and Volcarona, are also great teammates. Mega Meganium is also valued on rain teams that appreciate its unique defensive profile and ability to patch up rain's weaker matchups against Kingambit, Swords Dance Hisuian Samurott, and Hippowdon.

Defensive Pivot.description:
With great special bulk, solid typing, and the ability Regenerator, Galarian Slowking excels as one of the tier's best defensive pivots, able to repeatedly check a large number of special attackers, such as Primarina, Rotom-Wash, Mega Floette, and Mega Meganium, and punish them with a Sludge Bomb. Chilly Reception combined with its low Speed allows Galarian Slowking to pivot out and safely bring in a teammate. Future Sight, in combination with Chilly Reception, allows Galarian Slowking to apply delayed pressure to targets like Toxapex, Clefable, and Hippowdon, which teammates like Mega Lopunny and Sneasler can take advantage of. Psyshock can be used instead to immediately threaten Fighting- and Poison-types such as Sneasler, Glimmora, and Mega Dragalge while also doing the most damage to opposing Galarian Slowking. Thunder Wave can cripple threats like Volcarona, Hydreigon, and Mega Delphox for teammates that can take advantage of their lowered Speed. The combination of Ice Beam and Shuca Berry allows Galarian Slowking to withstand super effective Earthquakes from Garchomp and Dragonite and retaliate, often OHKOing offensive variants of the former, as well as KOing the latter with its Multiscale broken. Flamethrower can be used instead to do the most damage to Corviknight, Kingambit, and Aegislash, which can easily switch into Galarian Slowking’s other options. Toxic can put potential setup sweepers like Primarina, Skeledirge, Volcarona, and Mega Floette on a timer. Slack Off is another option that gives Galarian Slowking immediate recovery and helps it match up better against Quiver Dance Volcarona and Calm Mind Mega Floette. Colbur Berry lets Galarian Slowking stay in on its would-be checks, such as Meowscarada, Hydreigon, and Hisuian Samurott, and punish them with a Thunder Wave. Colbur Berry also lets Galarian Slowking survive a +2 Throat Chop from Sneasler and OHKO it with Psyshock. Sitrus Berry can be used as well for one-time recovery, helping Galarian Slowking remain healthy when it needs to stay in rather than pivot out. Kasib Berry is a more niche option that allows Galarian Slowking to stay in on threats like Dragapult, Ceruledge, and Annihilape and punish them with a Thunder Wave or Toxic.

Because of its defensive utility, Galarian Slowking can find its way on nearly any balance or bulky offense team. Offensive Fighting-types like Mega Lopunny, Blaziken, and Quaquaval can pressure the Dark- and Steel-types that commonly switch into Galarian Slowking while also appreciating its ability to bring them in safely with Chilly Reception and hit their would-be switch-ins like Toxapex, Mega Dragalge, and Clefable with Future Sight. They also appreciate Galarian Slowking's ability to absorb Toxic Spikes, which can otherwise hinder their longevity. Sweepers like Swords Dance Garchomp and Sneasler, as well as Nasty Plot Mega Delphox and Mega Raichu Y, also appreciate Galarian Slowking's ability to bring them in safely and allow them to get off a crucial boost. Galarian Slowking greatly appreciates partners like Garchomp, Hippowdon, Rotom-Wash, and Corviknight that can switch in on common physical attackers that threaten Galarian Slowking out, such as Excadrill, Hisuian Samurott, and Mega Metagross. Corviknight, in particular, can also clear entry hazards with Defog, allowing Galarian Slowking to switch in more frequently, while forming a great pivot core with U-turn. In return, Galarian Slowking checks Rotom-Wash, Mega Meganium, and Primarina for Corviknight. Dark-types like Kingambit, Hydreigon, and Hisuian Samurott are also valuable teammates, as they can easily switch in on Dark- and Ghost-type attacks from Meowscarada, Aegislash, and Dragapult, while Galarian Slowking can switch in on Fighting-type attacks. Slower attackers like Hisuian Samurott, Mega Meganium, and Aegislash also appreciate Galarian Slowking's ability to spread paralysis onto faster threats like Mega Metagross, Mega Lopunny, and Dragapult.

Bulky Swords Dance.description:
Mega Scizor uses its great defensive typing, high Attack, solid bulk, and powerful STAB Technician-boosted Bullet Punch to serve as an effective wallbreaker and cleaner, revenge killing weakened, fast, frail threats such as Dragapult, Mega Lopunny, and Sneasler. It can also find opportunities to set up Swords Dance against foes like non-Iron Defense Corviknight while checking wallbreakers like Mega Floette and Mega Metagross due to its bulk. Roost gives it much more longevity and more chances to set up. Close Combat tears down Steel-resistant Pokemon such as Archaludon, Excadrill, and most importantly Kingambit. Knock Off is an alternative to let Mega Scizor hit Aegislash, which is otherwise a huge roadblock, as well as Mega Delphox and Ceruledge on the switch in, which can shrug off its STAB Bullet Punch or Close Combat. 18 Speed SPs let Mega Scizor outpace Adamant Aegislash and Jolly Kingambit, while the HP SPs ensure that it doesn't get 2HKOed by Mega Floette's Moonblast and Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge.

Bulky offense and balance teams best appreciate Mega Scizor's ability to provide strong priority against foes like Sneasler. It also brings high defensive value, which allows it to answer dangerous wallbreakers like Mega Floette, Mega Mawile, and Mega Metagross. Mega Scizor's 4x weakness to Fire-type attacks from the likes of Ceruledge, Mega Delphox, Skeledirge, and Volcarona means that it appreciates teammates that can help against these particular foes. Water-types such as Hisuian Samurott, Rotom-Wash, and Primarina stand out, with Hisuian Samurott setting up Spikes and pressuring Ceruledge and Mega Delphox with Ceaseless Edge while using Flip Turn to bring Mega Scizor in safely against Fairy-types like Clefable and Mega Floette. Other entry hazard setters such as Garchomp and Glimmora make useful partners, with Stealth Rock chipping down the Fire-types that try to switch in on Mega Scizor and helping it guarantee the 2HKO on Dragapult. Dark-types such as Hydreigon and Meowscarada appreciate Mega Scizor's ability to dent Fairy-type foes with its STAB Bullet Punch. In return, Hydreigon can switch in on the Fire-type moves from the likes of Ceruledge and Mega Delphox while outpacing and pressuring the former with STAB Dark Pulse; Meowscarada helps against Water-types like Hisuian Samurott and Rotom-Wash. Special attackers like Volcarona, Hydreigon, and Primarina breaking down physically bulky Pokemon like Hippowdon and Rotom-Wash is appreciated by Mega Scizor, which, in return, can revenge kill faster threats to those special attackers like Garchomp and Sneasler.

Rain Sweeper.description:
Mega Swampert has always been a devastating staple on rain teams, with Swift Swim making it a fast wallbreaker and cleaner, and Champions gifting it Wave Crash to take its wallbreaking to a whole new level. Earthquake complements Wave Crash by threatening Water-resistant Pokemon such as Archaludon and Mega Dragalge. Ice Punch is used to snipe foes like Dragonite and Mega Meganium that resist Swampert's STAB moves, being able to comfortably 2HKO both of them from full. Alternatively, Stealth Rock can be used to gain value on the switches Swampert often forces, at the expense of no longer doing significant damage to Dragonite and Mega Meganium. Flip Turn allows Swampert to damage and pivot against walls like Rotom-Wash to bring in teammates like Archaludon. An Adamant nature is usually preferred in order to maximize Swampert's wallbreaking potential, having a favorable roll to 2HKO Rotom-Wash after Stealth Rock damage. However, a Jolly nature can be used to get the jump on Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon under rain, something Adamant Swampert is unable to do.

Mega Swampert fits exclusively on rain teams, so Pelipper is a mandatory teammate, with its slow U-turn giving Swampert safer opportunities to enter the field. Pelipper also appreciates Mega Swampert being immune to Electric-type attacks. Mega Swampert can struggle with threats like Rotom-Wash and Choice Scarf Meowscarada, which is why Archaludon is a fantastic partner, resisting their main attacks and threatening them with Draco Meteor while also taking advantage of rain with Electro Shot. Furthermore, Mega Swampert can help deal with Galarian Slowking, a wall that Archuladon can struggle against, limiting its ability to freely use Chilly Reception to remove rain. Other teammates that can take advantage of the rain, such as Basculegion-M and Hisuian Samurott, are great teammates, as together they can overwhelm shared checks like Rotom-Wash and Hydrapple. Hisuian Samurott can also lay down Spikes, which makes Swampert harder to pivot around. Hatterene is a good support partner, being able to bounce back entry hazards to keep Mega Swampert and Pelipper healthy. Furthermore, Hatterene can use Healing Wish to give Mega Swampert more opportunities to break the enemy team. Excadrill can also be an amazing support teammate, being able to use Rapid Spin to remove hazards as well as use Stealth Rock so that Swampert doesn't have to.

Wallbreaker.description:
Mega Mawile is a dangerous wallbreaker thanks to Huge Power, with its defensive typing and pre-Mega Intimidate giving it opportunities to come in against Pokemon such as Meowscarada and Hisuian Samurott before forcing switches. Swords Dance lets Mega Mawile overwhelm even sturdy physical walls, with +2 Thunder Punch OHKOing physically defensive Corviknight and Toxapex and +2 Play Rough OHKOing mixed defensive Hippowdon. Substitute instead takes advantage of the switches Mega Mawile forces to keep it protected as its checks come in; against physically defensive Leftovers Corviknight, for example, Thunder Punch 2HKOes it, while Brave Bird fails to break Mega Mawile's Substitute, allowing Mega Mawile to remain protected and continue pressuring the opposing team. Substitute can also protect Mega Mawile from status moves such as Rotom-Wash's Will-O-Wisp when used as Rotom-Wash switches in. Knock Off provides more generally useful coverage, OHKOing non-Colbur Berry Galarian Slowking and Aegislash as well as heavily punishing Colbur Berry variants while removing items from other switch-ins. Once Mega Evolved, Mega Mawile can stomach a Blaze Kick from Mega Staraptor and a Close Combat from Mega Lopunny and OHKO them in return with Play Rough. Sucker Punch makes up for Mega Mawile's poor Speed, OHKOing Dragapult and picking off weakened faster foes. 21 Speed SPs let Mega Mawile outspeed uninvested Corviknight and Kingambit.

Mega Mawile fits well on bulky offense and balance teams while also fitting naturally on Sticky Web offense. Hisuian Samurott is an excellent partner, setting Spikes with Ceaseless Edge to wear down Mega Mawile's switch-ins, while in return, Mega Mawile can switch into Choice Scarf Meowscarada's common attacks and OHKO it with Play Rough. Garchomp provides Stealth Rock support, notably breaking Dragonite's Multiscale so Mega Mawile can reliably OHKO it with Play Rough, while appreciating Mega Mawile pressuring Corviknight. Araquanid can set Sticky Web to offset Mega Mawile's poor Speed and reduce its reliance on Sucker Punch while also helping against Blaziken. Hatterene deters opposing entry hazards with Magic Bounce without removing its teammates' Spikes or Sticky Web, can restore a worn-down Mega Mawile with Healing Wish, and checks faster threats such as Mega Lopunny and Choice Scarf Hydreigon. Galarian Slowking helps cover Mega Meganium, Mega Clefable, and Volcarona, which can threaten Mega Mawile with Fire-type moves such as Weather Ball, Flamethrower, and Fiery Dance, while Chilly Reception can safely bring Mega Mawile in as foes such as Hisuian Samurott, Aegislash, and opposing Galarian Slowking switch into it. Mega Mawile's poor Speed and weaknesses to Ground and Fire leave it vulnerable to Garchomp, Excadrill, Hippowdon, and Blaziken when Sucker Punch cannot bail it out. On bulkier teams, Corviknight can switch into Ground-type attacks from Garchomp and Excadrill while removing Spikes with Defog, whereas Primarina and Aqua Jet users such as Hisuian Samurott and Paldean Tauros-W can revenge kill Blaziken. Dragonite is particularly useful on offensive teams, switching into Earthquake from Ground-types and checking Fire-types such as Blaziken and Volcarona while appreciating Mega Mawile breaking through physical walls like Corvikight for it.

All-out Attacker.description:
Mega Metagross works as an amazing wallbreaker and cleaner in the tier thanks to its high Attack stat, ability Tough Claws, and diverse movepool. Psychic Fangs allows Mega Metagross to 2HKO common defensive Pokemon like Rotom-Wash and Toxapex, as well as threatening an OHKO on Volcarona at the cost of a potential burn from Flame Body. Meteor Mash is able to hit Fairy-types like Clefable, Hatterene, and Mega Meganium super effectively. Bullet Punch, while weaker against Fairy-types, allows Mega Metagross to revenge kill weakened threats like Garchomp and Mega Lopunny after they use Scale Shot and Close Combat. Earthquake is used to hit Aegislash, Excadrill, and Archaludon super effectively, as they otherwise end up walling Metagross. Thunder Punch allows it to hit Corviknight and Hisuian Samurott, as well as OHKOing defensive Pelipper. Ice Punch comes at the cost of another necessary coverage move but can be very useful in eliminating Dragonite and Garchomp. Similarly, Body Press and Hammer Arm are also options that can be used to surprise and OHKO Kingambit, and they can bypass Shuca Berry on Excadrill and Archaludon. Jolly is the preferred nature to let Mega Metagross outspeed common Pokemon like Garchomp, Mega Floette, and Mega Glimmora as well as Speed tie with Mega Staraptor. Before Mega Evolving, Clear Body helps Metagross not be affected by Sticky Web or Mawile's and Staraptor's Intimidate.

Mega Metagross fits best on bulky offense and balance teams where its offensive prowess and coverage can help them either make progress or clean late-game. Metagross often wants to come out against specially bulky Pokemon that aren't equipped to take on its strong physical moves, such as Galarian Slowking, Mega Dragalge, and Toxapex. Therefore, it appreciates being paired with pivots like Rotom-Wash and Primarina that often force in these Pokemon for it to take advantage of Rotom-Wash and Primarina can use Volt Switch and Flip Turn to bring Metagross in against these Pokemon. Rotom-Wash in particular has amazing synergy with Metagross, as it can switch into Ground-type attacks from Garchomp and Mega Swampert and Fire-type attacks from Ceruledge, cripple the former two with Will-O-Wisp, and threaten Ceruledge with Hydro Pump. Entry hazards help Mega Metagross wallbreak easily, so Pokemon like Hippowdon, Hisuian Samurott, and Garchomp are excellent partners. This chip damage is particularly useful for whittling physically defensive Corviknight into range of Thunder Punch and opposing bulky Garchomp into range of Ice Punch. Hisuian Samurott and Garchomp can also pressure defensive checks like Corviknight and Skarmory with Swords Dance-boosted Ceaseless Edge and Fire Fang, making it easier for Metagross to clean up. Mega Metagross can easily be worn down by hazards, which makes hazard removal from partners like Corviknight and Excadrill very helpful. Corviknight also acts as a switch-in to Ground-type attacks aimed at Metagross and is able to check Kingambit with Body Press. Meanwhile, Excadrill can threaten Steel-types like Archaludon and Mega Mawile, freeing up some of Metagross's need for coverage. Since Mega Metagross can be walled by Mega Scizor and other Steel-types depending on its coverage, Fire-types like Volcarona, Ceruledge, and Rotom-Heat are considered good partners. The former two also love its help in dealing with Toxapex as well as chipping Rotom-Wash and Garchomp down. Metagross doesn't like taking on super effective priority moves like Shadow Sneak and Sucker Punch, specifically from Kingambit. That's why fast Dark-types like Hydreigon and Meowscarada and Fighting-types like Quaquaval and Sneasler are all greatly appreciated as teammates.

Three Attacks.description:
Mega Staraptor serves as a fantastic cleaner with its great Speed outpacing key Pokemon such as Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott, good offensive typing, a high Attack stat, and high Base Power moves. Its access to Contrary also makes it capable of boosting its defenses with Close Combat, making it very hard to take down, even for offensive teams. With one Close Combat, Mega Staraptor is able to survive notable super effective hits such as Meowscarada's Triple Axel and Mega Delphox's Psyshock. With two Close Combats, it can also survive Mega Floette's Moonblast and Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon. Blaze Kick hits Aegislash, Corviknight, and Mega Scizor while also being a valuable attack against Steel-types after Close Combat's PP has been drained. Roost grants Mega Staraptor longevity, synergizing well with the defense boosts garnered from Close Combat, making it a reliable check to Pokemon such as Hisuian Samurott, Kingambit, and Blaziken. As well as this, Roost allows you to manage the recoil from Brave Bird more easily.

Mega Staraptor fits well on offense teams where it appreciates teammates such as Primarina, Volcarona, and Swords Dance Ceruledge that are able to soften physical walls such as Corviknight and Hippowdon into range of its attacks. In return, Mega Staraptor deals with priority Pokemon such as Sucker Punch Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit as well as Bullet Punch Mega Scizor that would revenge kill its sweeper partners. Mega Staraptor also fits well on entry hazard stacking and Sticky Web teams where Contrary allows it to punish Defog, while Sticky Web allows Mega Staraptor to outspeed faster Pokemon such as Mega Raichu Y. Offensive hazard setters such as Stealth Rock Garchomp and Glimmora as well as Ceaseless Edge Hisuian Samurott work well with Mega Staraptor, as their hazards chip down physical walls into range of its attacks. In return, they appreciate Mega Staraptor's ability to deter Defog. Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit work well as offensive partners, eliminating Ghost-types such as Aegislash and Dragapult that are immune to Close Combat while also switching into Psychic-type attacks such as Mega Delphox's Psyshock. Galarian Slowking serves as a defensive partner that can switch into Fairy-type attacks from the likes of Mega Floette, temporarily sponge Electric-type moves from Mega Raichu Y, and be a good switch-in to status moves that would otherwise debilitate Mega Staraptor. In return, Mega Staraptor is able to sponge Dark-type moves from Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit while using its Ground-type immunity to switch into Earthquake from Garchomp and Excadrill.

All-Out Attacker.description:
Mega Lopunny can effectively carry out the roles of wallbreaker, cleaner, and revenge killer all at once. Fake Out can pick off weakened threats such as Scale Shot Garchomp, Weak Armor Ceruledge, and Sneasler. Mach Punch fulfills a similar function, hitting foes resistant to Normal such as Mega Barbaracle and Sucker Punch Kingambit and, when used in conjunction with Fake Out, further improving Mega Lopunny's revenge-killing capabilities. Triple Axel is its strongest option to hit common Dragon-types such as Garchomp, Dragonite, and Mega Dragalge, as well as other Fighting-resistant foes such as Mega Staraptor and Mega Meganium. U-turn allows Mega Lopunny to generate momentum for its team while hitting switch-ins for decent damage, which is particularly useful against Galarian Slowking. Mega Kick can be run to hit specific answers such as Volcarona, Toxapex, and Galarian Slowking, which are otherwise problematic, but its low accuracy is a drawback. A Jolly nature is preferred to outspeed the likes of Mega Raichu Y, Mega Delphox, and Sneasler before Unburden activates. However, Mega Lopunny can afford to run an Adamant nature to maximize its wallbreaking potential and pick off threats from higher HP ranges with Fake Out and Mach Punch.

Mega Lopunny is a fantastic hit-and-run attacker for offense and balance teams alike, providing a fail-safe against dangerous setup sweepers thanks to its two priority moves without giving up its sheer wallbreaking power. It is quite frail, so teammates providing safe entry points, such as Rotom-Wash or Galarian Slowking, are appreciated. The latter in particular is an amazing partner, providing Future Sight support, absorb Toxic Spikes, and deal with common Fairy-types like Clefable, Primarina, and Mega Floette. In return, Mega Lopunny threatens common Steel-types like Aegislash, Excadrill, and Kingambit. Dark-type attackers like Hydreigon, Kingambit, and Hisuian Samurott are great at pressuring Psychic-types. Hisuian Samurott also sets up Spikes with Ceaseless Edge, greatly enhancing Mega Lopunny's late-game cleaning capabilities. Garchomp is another strong teammate: its tank sets lay down Spikes and Stealth Rock while chipping foes with Rough Skin, whereas its more offense-oriented sets can overwhelm common switch-ins such as Corviknight or Rotom-Wash. Garchomp is also able to threaten defensive Poison-types such as Toxapex, Mega Dragalge, and Galarian Slowking with Earthquake. Hatterene bounces back Sticky Web, can paralyze exceptionally fast foes with Nuzzle, prevents healing attempts with Psychic Noise, and can give a worn-down Mega Lopunny a second chance thanks to Healing Wish, which is especially useful against Flame Body Volcarona. Steel-type Pokemon able to switch into repeated Psychic- and Fairy-type attacks, such as Aegislash and Corviknight, help Mega Lopunny pivot around its counters. They also support Mega Lopunny, with Aegislash forming a wallbreaking core and providing a secondary source of priority through Shadow Sneak, and Corviknight removing entry hazards and creating pivoting opportunities with U-turn. Dragonite is appealing as a switch-in to Earthquake, which offense teams are often weak to; it also provides a secondary source of priority through Extreme Speed and can use Dragon Dance to sweep through teams weakened by Mega Lopunny. For bulkier teams, Hippowdon is a great catch-all answer to physical attackers that threaten Mega Lopunny and provides significant chip damage through Stealth Rock, sand, and Whirlwind.

Mixed Life Orb.description:
Garchomp can invest into its Special Attack to become a highly threatening mixed attacker, capable of breaking most defensive cores while also finding many opportunities to switch in thanks to its great defensive typing and natural bulk. Draco Meteor functions as a great neutral option, 2HKOing foes like Rotom-Wash, Glimmora, and Mega Staraptor while also OHKOing Meowscarada and Hisuian Samurott after entry hazard chip damage. Flamethrower allows Garchomp to 2HKO Corviknight and Skarmory, which are unphased by Garchomp's other options. Due to the fact that Garchomp greatly threatens common hazard removal options like Corviknight, Excadrill, and Glimmora, it is great at setting Stealth Rock and making sure the hazard stays up for its teammates to take advantage of the passive chip damage. If the team has a different Stealth Rock setter, like Glimmora or Excadrill, Poison Jab can be run instead to threaten Fairy-types like Mega Meganium and Mega Clefable, which can otherwise withstand Garchomp's attacks. A Life Orb allows Garchomp to reach important benchmarks like 2HKOing Corviknight with Flamethrower and OHKOing Mega Meganium with Poison Jab.

Mixed Garchomp is one of the most defining Pokemon on offensive teams and can easily find its place on nearly any team thanks to its ability to break defensive cores while also keeping entry hazards up. It greatly appreciates Water- and Grass-type attackers, like Primarina, Rotom-Wash, Mega Meganium, and Meowscarada, that can apply pressure to mixed defensive Hippowdon, which can survive two Draco Meteors and recover off the damage. Hisuian Samurott is also a great partner, as its Spikes allow Garchomp to reach important benchmarks like KOing opposing Hisuian Samurott with Draco Meteor, OHKOing Mega Dragalge and offensive Kingambit with Earthquake, and 2HKOing Hatterene with Earthquake. In return, Hisuian Samurott appreciates Garchomp's ability to pressure Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, which can otherwise give it trouble. Garchomp also appreciates support from Healing Wish users like Hatterene, as it can get worn down quickly from hazards and constant Life Orb recoil. Galarian Slowking, Rotom-Wash, and Corviknight are great teammates, as they can bring Garchomp in safely with their pivoting moves, reducing the amount of damage it would otherwise take from switching in while also allowing it to fall back on them after a Draco Meteor Special Attack drop. Galarian Slowking can also switch in on Fairy-types that commonly force Garchomp out, like Primarina, Clefable, and Mega Floette. Additionally, Corviknight can switch into threats like Mega Lopunny, Meowscarada, and Dragapult that can attempt to revenge kill Garchomp. Many sweepers like Swords Dance Scizor, Sneasler, and Mega Mawile, as well as Bulk Up Annihilape, appreciate its ability to pressure the aforementioned Corviknight and Rotom-Wash.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Garchomp is blessed with a Speed tier that allows it to outrun common sweepers such as Volcarona and Mega Charizard X after a Speed boost, as well as other fast attackers such as Mega Raichu Y and Mega Delphox, and swiftly KOes them with its powerful STAB moves and coverage. It also lets it avoid having to Speed tie with Mega Floette. Outrage is an incredibly powerful STAB option that can clean up games once Pokemon that resist or are immune to it have been dealt with. Stone Edge targets common Ground-immune foes such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Delphox, and Mega Clefable. It also OHKOes Volcarona, a threat that Earthquake does not OHKO. Rock Tomb is a much more accurate option that still OHKOes offensive Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y. Its Speed drop can also leave setup sweepers such as Dragonite and Mega Froslass easier for teammates to revenge kill. However, Rock Tomb cannot OHKO Mega Delphox, even after Stealth Rock, and cannot 2HKO Mega Clefable. Poison Jab is the strongest option available to hit Fairy-types, most notably OHKOing Mega Meganium, which would otherwise counter Garchomp, after Stealth Rock damage. It also does slightly more damage to Fairy-types than an unresisted Earthquake, which can be relevant when looking to KO foes such as Mega Floette and Clefable. Stealth Rock may let Garchomp act as a secondary setter if its team already handles Mega Meganium effectively, though locking into it gives up momentum.

Choice Scarf Garchomp can easily find its place on offense and balance teams looking for solid Speed control to deal with the likes of Volcarona, Mega Charizard X, and Mega Raichu Y. It also boasts a solid defensive typing that lets it switch into various attacks it resists or is immune to. Corviknight is Garchomp's main obstacle when trying to make progress, so teammates most apt at pressuring it and making progress against it, such as Black Glasses Hisuian Samurott, Rotom-Wash, and Shadow Ball Aegislash, are of utmost importance. Defensive teammates Garchomp can fall back on after being locked into a move, such as Corviknight, Galarian Slowking, and Rotom-Wash, are highly valuable. They also have the added benefit of having pivoting moves to bring Garchomp back in safely. In return, Garchomp handles their answers, such as Mega Raichu Y, Excadrill, and Mega Dragalge, respectively. Galarian Slowking in particular is one of the rare switch-ins to Mega Meganium, and is, for this reason, one of Choice Scarf Garchomp's best teammates. Stealth Rock setters such as Glimmora, Clefable, and Tinkaton are a great fit to fix various key interactions, such as breaking Dragonite's and Mega Dragonite's Multiscale, breaking Focus Sash from Ceruledge, and putting Mega Meganium in range of Poison Jab, so Garchomp can reliably KO them. Garchomp appreciates particularly strong physical wallbreakers such as Blaziken, Mega Mawile, and Mega Metagross overpowering physical walls such as Corviknight, Hippowdon, and Clefable, so that Garchomp may clean up late-game. In return, Garchomp can switch into Fire-type attacks targeting the latter two. Offensive Poison- and Steel-type teammates such as Mega Glimmora, Mega Metagross, and Mega Mawile are able to proactively switch into Fairy-types such as Mega Floette and Clefable and immediately pressure them, though they must be careful of Mega Meganium's coverage options.

Mixed Wall.description:
Hippowdon is a sturdy wall that differentiates itself from other common Ground-types thanks to its access to reliable recovery in Slack Off and its ability to stave off some of the scariest wallbreakers in the tier that otherwise have great matchups against slower teams. Such threats include Mega Glimmora and Mega Metagross, as well as Mega Charizard Y and Archaludon thanks to Sand Stream removing opposing weather. Whirlwind forces Stealth Rock damage onto the opposing team and phazes dangerous sweepers such as Mega Staraptor and Dragonite. The SP investment allows Hippowdon to tank two unboosted Draco Meteors or one +1 Draco Meteor from Archaludon, two Flamethrowers from Mega Charizard Y, two Draco Meteors from mixed Life Orb Garchomp, and two unboosted Meteor Mashes or Ice Punches from Mega Metagross. Leftovers and Sitrus Berry guarantee Hippowdon can reliably achieve these feats, even after Stealth Rock chip damage. Holding no item is an option if both Leftovers and Sitrus Berry are already taken by teammates, as doing so ensures that Hippowdon can reliably switch into Poltergeist users such as Ceruledge and Aegislash.

This set's ability to handle key wallbreakers makes it a good fit on bulkier teams ranging from balance to stall. Since Hippowdon invites opposing Defog Corviknight in frequently, teammates able to make the most out of that matchup, such as Shadow Ball Aegislash, Ceruledge, and Mega Meganium, are important to have. Poison-type walls such as Galarian Slowking, Mega Dragalge, and Poison Jab Toxapex take pressure off of Hippowdon and are excellent answers to Mega Meganium, as well as Mega Clefable, which completely stops Hippowdon from making progress. They can also set Toxic Spikes, which makes Whirlwind much more irritating. In the same vein, Spikes setters such as Hisuian Samurott and Meowscarada are good teammates, increasing the chip damage Whirlwind can accumulate. Corviknight is a key partner, acting as a secondary physical wall and using Defog to remove the Spikes and Toxic Spikes that would otherwise cut into Hippowdon's longevity and prevent it from switching into key wallbreakers. Rotom-Wash brings momentum with Volt Switch, is able to switch into Mega Swampert, and makes progress against Corviknight. Blaziken, Ceruledge, and Mega Mawile are incredible wallbreakers that can easily dismantle defensive teams and have a chance to OHKO Hippowdon after a Swords Dance. As such, if running Hippowdon on a stall team, Skeledirge, Unaware Clefable, and Ditto are invaluable teammates to deal with them.

Special Attacker.description:
Mega Froslass secures a niche in the tier as a solid wallbreaker thanks to its unique offensive coverage as well as great Speed and Special Attack. Its ability, Snow Warning, gives it a Defense boost, allowing it to survive Meowscarada's Knock Off even after Stealth Rock chip damage, as well as Shadow Sneak from +2 Adamant Ceruledge. Additionally, with Snow Warning, Blizzard can bypass accuracy checks, letting Mega Froslass threaten many common foes like Garchomp, Dragonite, Mega Meganium, and Corviknight. Shadow Ball allows it to damage common Ice-resistant foes like Aegislash, Mega Metagross, and Ceruledge as well as bulky Pokemon like Galarian Slowking super effectively. Nasty Plot lets Mega Froslass become an insanely powerful wallbreaker; after a boost, it OHKOes physically defensive Clefable and Corviknight. Thunderbolt can be used to hit Greninja and Hisuian Samurott super effectively, which otherwise resist Mega Froslass's STAB moves. Will-O-Wisp can be useful to cripple physically offensive answers to Mega Froslass such as Kingambit, Tyranitar, and Mega Scizor. It also synergizes very well with the Defense boost provided by snow; Mega Froslass is able to survive a Meteor Mash from a burned Mega Metagross when snow is active, and Bullet Punch's damage output is greatly reduced when Mega Scizor is affected by Will-O-Wisp. This makes it easier for Mega Froslass to pressure them with Shadow Ball. Aurora Veil is another option that lets Mega Froslass have an easier time boosting with Nasty Plot and allows its teammates to enter the field more safely.

Mega Froslass finds its way on all types of offense teams that appreciate its ability to break common defensive cores. Physical sweepers such as Dragonite, Kingambit, and Quaquaval benefit from Mega Froslass pressuring physically bulky Pokemon like Clefable, Corviknight, and Rotom-Wash as well as the damage reduction provided by Aurora Veil. Quaquaval, in particular, shines as a partner due to its ability to break past common Dark- and Fire-types like Hisuian Samurott, Kingambit, and Volcarona that Mega Froslass struggles against while also bringing Mega Froslass in with Flip Turn and removing entry hazards, especially Stealth Rock, with Rapid Spin. Other entry hazard removers like Corviknight, Excadrill, and Glimmora are all great partners as well, with Corviknight providing Mega Froslass with safe entry via its slow U-turn. On the other hand, entry hazards of your own help Mega Froslass break its foes more easily, so hazard setters like Garchomp and Hisuian Samurott along with the aforementioned Excadrill and Glimmora work extremely well as teammates, with Stealth Rock ensuring that Mega Froslass's Thunderbolt OHKOes Greninja and Hisuian Samurott. Hatterene is another useful partner, providing paralysis support with Nuzzle to slow down faster threats such as Dragapult, Greninja, and Meowscarada as well as entry hazard control with Magic Bounce. It can also check Mega Lopunny decently well, which Mega Froslass benefits from. Bulky Water-types like Toxapex, Rotom-Wash, and Primarina that can switch into repeated Fire-type attacks from the likes of Blaziken, Ceruledge, and Volcarona are also greatly appreciated as teammates.

Defensive Pivot.description:
With serviceable bulk, a fantastic defensive typing supported by Levitate, and a good utility movepool, Rotom-Wash can function as a great defensive pivot. Hydro Pump threatens Fire- and Ground-types, like Ceruledge, Blaziken, Garchomp, and Hippowdon. Volt Switch serves as Rotom-Wash's primary Electric-type STAB move, hitting Flying- and Water-types like Corviknight, Hisuian Samurott, and Primarina while also allowing it to safely bring in a teammate. Will-O-Wisp can immediately threaten most physical attackers, such as Dragonite, Kingambit, Mega Metagross, and Mega Staraptor. Pain Split, combined with Rotom-Wash's low HP stat, allows it to recover health against its common switch-ins, like Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge, ensuring it stays healthy throughout the game. Rest, alongside Chesto Berry, can be used instead as a more immediate recovery option. Sitrus Berry gives Rotom-Wash a one-time recovery option instead, preventing it from spending a turn using Pain Split or Rest. Leftovers can alternatively be used to let Rotom-Wash have a more passive recovery option while also taking advantage of passive foes like Galarian Slowking and Clefable. Rotom-Wash can also opt for no item to let it best stand up to Poltergeist users like Ceruledge and Aegislash, at the cost of giving up item-based recovery. 7 Speed SPs allow Rotom-Wash to outspeed Adamant Aegislash and Jolly Kingambit to potentially get off a Will-O-Wisp or pivot out to a teammate.

Thanks to its defensive utility as well as its ability to pivot to a teammate, Rotom-Wash works well on both balance and bulky offense teams. Special walls like Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge make great teammates, as they can switch in against the special attackers that commonly force it out, like Primarina, Mega Meganium, Mega Raichu Y, and Mega Floette. In return, Rotom-Wash can switch in against and burn foes that threaten them, like Garchomp, Dragonite, Hisuian Samurott, and Mega Metagross. Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge also have excellent type synergy with Rotom-Wash and can form a great pivot core with their access to Chilly Reception and Flip Turn, respectively. Rotom-Wash also appreciates support from Fairy-type attackers like Primarina, Mega Floette, and Mega Meganium in order to pressure Dragon-types like Dragapult, Hydreigon, and Mega Dragonite, which resist both of Rotom-Wash's attacks. Physical wallbreakers like Blaziken, Dragonite, Mega Metagross, and Mega Lopunny are also good teammates, as they can take advantage of Galarian Slowking, Mega Meganium, and Mega Dragalage, which can commonly switch in on Rotom-Wash. Due to the fact that Rotom-Wash greatly threatens Corviknight, physical attackers like Meowscarada, Scizor, and Excadrill appreciate its presence while also being brought in safely by its Volt Switch. Ghost-types like Dragapult and Aegislash also appreciate Rotom-Wash's ability to threaten burn on Dark-type attackers like Hisuian Samurott, Meowscarada, and Kingambit, while they can do super effective damage to Galarian Slowking in return. Rotom-Wash struggles against Mold Breaker Excadrill, which can hit it through Levitate; therefore, Corviknight, Garchomp, and Hippowdon make great teammates, with Corviknight switching into Excadrill while providing Defog and U-turn support and the latter two immediately threatening it with their Ground-type STAB moves.

Bulky Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance alongside a boosting item allows Hisuian Samurott to take its damage output to new highs, functioning as a wallbreaker and sweeper off the strength of its powerful Dark-type STAB moves. Sharpness-boosted Ceaseless Edge is one of the strongest Dark-type moves in the tier, and it also sets Spikes that make progress even against Pokemon like Mega Meganium, Primarina, and Mega Floette that resist the move. This not only accentuates Hisuian Samurott's own gameplan of taking down teams but also supports its teammates in the process. Sucker Punch circumvents Hisuian Samurott's middling Speed and allows it to handle offensive threats such as Dragapult, Mega Delphox, and Mega Metagross; entry hazards allow even unboosted Sucker Punch to OHKO Pokemon like Mega Raichu Y. Black Glasses helps with Hisuian Samurott's damage output, helping it OHKO bulky foes such as Rotom-Wash with a +2 Ceaseless Edge after minor chip damage and fast offensive ones such as Mega Glimmora with a +2 Sucker Punch after entry hazard damage. With hazard removers like Corviknight, especially if Hisuian Samurott's set is unknown to the opponent, Hisuian Samurott can use them as an opportunity to set up a Swords Dance and either use Encore to lock the target into a disadvantageous move, allowing for further usage of Swords Dance, or block status moves with Taunt to maintain hazards or prevent setup. Sacred Sword is another option, allowing Hisuian Samurott to OHKO certain Pokemon that resist its Dark-type moves such as Kingambit and opposing Hisuian Samurott; its secondary effect allows Hisuian Samurott to break through Archaludon regardless of how many Defense boosts from Stamina it has accrued. Hisuian Samurott's SP spread maximizes its Attack, uses 8 Speed SPs to outspeed Jolly Kingambit and neutral-natured Aegislash, and invests the remainder in HP.

Hisuian Samurott's potent offensive typing and ability to immediately threaten foes or force progress makes it a great piece on a variety of archetypes, as it helps out against some of the most effective offensive Pokemon such as Aegislash, Ceruledge, and, if it can lock it into a disadvantageous move with Encore or has Sacred Sword, Kingambit. Stealth Rock users such as Garchomp and Excadrill synergize with Hisuian Samurott greatly, being immune to Electric-type attacks from Pokemon such as Mega Raichu Y and Rotom-Wash while assisting in an entry hazard stacking strategy. Other Stealth Rock users, such as Glimmora, can work quite effectively alongside Hisuian Samurott on more hyper offensive builds. With its bulk, this set works as an effective switch-in to Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking; this quality assists potent specially offensive teammates such as Volcarona, Mega Meganium, and Mega Floette. Such teammates, in return, help out Hisuian Samurott by dealing with Fighting-type threats such as Mega Lopunny, which threatens to outspeed and OHKO Hisuian Samurott. Fellow Dark-types such as Kingambit, Meowscarada, and Hydreigon appreciate Hisuian Samurott wearing down shared answers such as Corviknight and Hatterene.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf allows Hisuian Samurott to compress roles as both speed control and a strong Spikes setter for balance and bulky offense teams due to its access to Ceaseless Edge. The item gives Hisuian Samurott the jump on faster foes such as Dragapult and Mega Delphox, allowing it to revenge kill them with Ceaseless Edge; Mega Raichu Y and Mega Metagross can also be picked off once weakened. Flip Turn allows Hisuian Samurott to act as a pivot against switch-ins such as Clefable, Corviknight, and Mega Meganium. Razor Shelloffers frequent Defense drops and higher Base Power, but Aqua Cutter is a viable alternative due to it not making contact against Rough Skin Garchomp as well as its high critical hit rate and perfect accuracy. Sacred Sword serves as coverage against Kingambit, Hydreigon, and opposing Hisuian Samurott. Aqua Jet allows Hisuian Samurott to snipe frailer foes that outspeed it, such as boosted Volcarona and Blaziken. It also allows Hisuian Samurott to get around Mach Punch Mega Lopunny if weakened. Finally, Knock Off is a more niche alternative to the two, removing valuable held items such as Dragonite's Lum Berry and Clefable's Leftovers and allowing Hisuian Samurott to discourage direct switch-ins more.

Hisuian Samurott's entry hazard-setting capability gives it major utility for its team, which makes Stealth Rock setters such as Garchomp and Glimmora valuable partners. Stealth Rock is especially key for chipping Flying-types such as Corviknight and Dragonite, which avoid Spikes, and Garchomp can help Hisuian Samurott overwhelm shared checks in Corviknight and Clefable. While Hisuian Samurott can set up Spikes quite easily, it struggles to maintain them versus the aforementioned Corviknight, making Fire-types such as Volcarona, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge all great teammates to discourage Corviknight from switching into Hisuian Samurott. Ceruledge and Annihilape can also block a predicted Rapid Spin from Excadrill. Other wallbreakers and cleaners such as Mega Lopunny, Sneasler, and Kingambit all appreciate Hisuian Samurott's hazard support, and the former two additionally appreciate it beating Psychic-types such as Galarian Slowking and Mega Delphox; in return, they beat Dark-types such as opposing Hisuian Samurott and Hydreigon. Kingambit appreciates overwhelmed checks such as Sneasler, while it can pick off foes faster than Hisuian Samurott, such as boosted Mega Charizard X. Galarian Slowking can serve as a switch-in to Fairy-types such as Primarina, Clefable, and Mega Floette while supporting Hisuian Samurott with Future Sight. In return, Hisuian Samurott can threaten the Ghost- and Ground-types that Galarian Slowking may bring in, such as Aegislash and Excadrill. Finally, Mega Meganium is a useful ally, doing well against the aforementioned Primarina and Quaquaval while overwhelming a shared check in Corviknight. In return, Hisuian Samurott can slice past Galarian Slowking and Ceruledge, which Mega Meganium does not like dealing with.

Wallbreaker.description:
Thanks to its insanely high Speed and Special Attack as well as its solid type coverage, Mega Delphox works as one of the tier's deadliest wallbreakers and cleaners. Flamethrower is the preferred choice of Fire-type STAB move because of its perfect accuracy, but Fire Blast can be run, at the expense of that accuracy, for greater damage output, which lets Mega Delphox have a chance to 2HKO no bulk Hisuian Samurott and OHKO Careful Excadrill after Stealth Rock. Psyshock is used to deal more damage to common special walls, most notably to OHKO Galarian Slowking and 32 HP Primarina after Nasty Plot and Stealth Rock damage, as well as to OHKO Mega Dragalge after Stealth Rock. Dazzling Gleam is used to hit Dragon- and Dark-types like Hydreigon, Hisuian Samurott, and Greninja that otherwise resist or are immune to Mega Delphox's STAB moves. Substitute is a solid option that can ease prediction, avoid status from the likes of Galarian Slowking, Hatterene, and Toxapex, and avoid Sucker Punch from Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit, though it does come at the cost of either Nasty Plot's breaking potential or Dazzling Gleam's coverage. Similarly, Encore is a utility option that can be used to lock opponents into non-damaging moves, giving Delphox free turns to use Nasty Plot. It can also situationally work well in tandem with Mega Delphox's ability Levitate, locking Pokemon like Garchomp into Earthquake. Focus Blast and Grass Knot are niche coverage choices that can be used to deal with specific walls like Tyranitar, Slowbro, and Slowking. Timid is the preferred nature to outspeed Mega Raichu Y, Greninja, and Sneasler. 1 SP in Defense and HP lets Mega Delphox survive Shadow Sneak from Adamant Spell Tag Aegislash and Adamant Life Orb Ceruledge.

Mega Delphox fits best on offense, bulky offense, and balance teams that can provide ample support in the form of pivoting and entry hazard control for Mega Delphox to effectively break and clean late-game. Hence, Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Corviknight are solid partners, as they are able to bring Mega Delphox safely onto the field using Chilly Reception and U-turn, respectively. Corviknight also supports Mega Delphox by removing Stealth Rock using Defog; similarly, other Stealth Rock removers like Excadrill and Glimmora can also make for good partners. On the other hand, Mega Delphox itself appreciates hazards that help chip the opposing team down and let Mega Delphox achieve, for instance, a guaranteed OHKO on Hisuian Samurott using Dazzling Gleam and a guaranteed OHKO on Galarian Slowking using +2 Psyshock. For that reason, Pokemon like Garchomp, Glimmora, and Hisuian Samurott are crucial teammates. Bulky partners that can deal with faster threats like Mega Lopunny and Dragapult, such as Primarina, Toxapex, and Clefable, are appreciated. Mega Delphox is often revenge killed using super effective priority moves like Shadow Sneak and Sucker Punch from Aegislash, Ceruledge, and Kingambit; therefore, Dark-types that can handle these moves like Hisuian Samurott, Hydreigon, and Meowscarda are all great teammates. Meowscarada, in particular, has amazing offensive synergy with Mega Delphox, as it has U-turn to pivot out against common Steel-type switch-ins like Corviknight, Scizor, and Mega Metagross to bring Mega Delphox in, giving Mega Delphox opportunities to either set up freely or deal a lot of damage. Meowscarada also pressures physically bulky Rotom-Wash, which Delphox may struggle against. Skeledirge is another Pokemon that walls Mega Delphox, due to Unaware, so Pokemon that can easily pressure it like Primarina, Rotom-Wash, and Hydreigon are appreciated. The former two also help in tanking Water-type attacks aimed at Mega Delphox. Finally, late-game sweepers that can take advantage of Mega Delphox weakening the opposing team like Kingambit, Dragonite, and Sneasler all work well as teammates.

Bulky Calm Mind.description:
Mega Floette can run heavy Defense investment to leverage its fantastic defensive typing and multiple recovery options to act as a durable tank and sweeper. This bulk investment allows Mega Floette to avoid OHKOs from threatening attacks such as Sneasler's Dire Claw and Blaziken's Flare Blitz and then strike back. Calm Mind increases Draining Kiss's recovery and makes Mega Floette extremely difficult to take down on the special side. Synthesis acts as a secondary recovery option to help against threats that take little damage from Draining Kiss such as Galarian Slowking and Mega Delphox. Moonblast is a strong secondary attacking option with much higher damage output than Draining Kiss. It helps take down weakened threats before they can act or simply punches holes into frailer teams with no solid switch-in, scoring an OHKO on offensive Garchomp and Annihilape while having a small chance to OHKO uninvested Archaludon. Alternatively, Substitute and Misty Terrain prevent poison spreaders such as Galarian Slowking and Mega Dragalge from putting Mega Floette on a timer; this preparation may allow Mega Floette to beat Galarian Slowking.

This bulky Mega Floette variant can act as a solid switch-in to a wide array of key Pokemon such as Annihilape, Hisuian Samurott, most Garchomp variants, and Mega Lopunny. Balance and bulky offense teams especially enjoy Mega Floette's ability to both defensively answer Dark- and Fighting-types and easily threaten a sweep once key defensive answers such as Galarian Slowking, Toxapex, and Skeledirge are KOed. Mega Floette needs teammates that can put pressure on defensive Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon, especially Galarian Slowking and Toxapex. As such, Ground-type teammates such as Garchomp, Excadrill, and Hippowdon, are necessary. Dark-type attackers such as Hydreigon and Hisuian Samurott are able to put pressure on Galarian Slowking and Skeledirge, and the latter may set Spikes through Ceaseless Edge, chipping at grounded Steel-type foes such as Excadrill, Aegislash, and Mega Metagross. In return, Mega Floette can switch into Fighting-type attacks that threaten them. Hisuian Samurott is also capable of threatening a weakened Mega Metagross with Sucker Punch or Choice Scarf Ceaseless Edge. Mega Metagross is an extremely dangerous threat as a balance breaker that also beats Mega Floette. As such, Hippowdon is one of Mega Floette's best teammates as one of the few reliable switch-ins to Mega Metagross while threatening a strong Earthquake against Steel- and Poison-type foes. Since Mega Floette is particularly vulnerable to all entry hazards that can make it unable to switch into various attackers, hazard removal in the form of Corviknight, Scizor, or Excadrill is important; these Pokemon also switch into Poison- and Steel-type attacks. Grounded Poison-type teammates, such as Galarian Slowking, Toxapex, and Sneasler, can reliably clear Toxic Spikes, which otherwise heavily undermines Mega Floette's staying power. While decent with investment, Mega Floette's physical bulk is too low to reliably take on strong physical attackers that can hit Mega Floette for neutral or super effective damage such as offensive Garchomp, Mega Scizor, Sneasler, and Blaziken. Therefore, secondary physical walls such as Hippowdon and Corviknight for the first three, as well as Slowbro for Blaziken, alleviate a lot of pressure.

Shell Smash.description:
With access to Shell Smash and a good offensive typing, Mega Barbaracle functions as a niche but devastating sweeper. However, it can struggle to find safe opportunities to set up, and Stone Edge's shaky accuracy can cut a sweep short. Close Combat cleanly OHKOes some of the tier’s main walls like Corviknight, Rotom-Wash, and physically defensive Garchomp after a Shell Smash. Stone Edge lets Mega Barbaracle threaten foes that resist Close Combat, such as Hatterene and Magic Guard Clefable, while KOing Mega Staraptor and Dragonite through Multiscale after a boost. Shadow Claw allows Mega Barbaracle to OHKO Annihilape and Aegislash after a Shell Smash. Alternatively, Earthquake threatens Ground-weak foes such as Aegislash and can OHKO Toxapex at +2 after Stealth Rock, preventing it from removing Mega Barbaracle's boosts with Haze. An Adamant nature allows Mega Barbaracle to guarantee OHKOs on certain Pokemon like physically defensive Primarina, Garchomp, and Hippowdon after entry hazard chip damage. A Jolly nature can be used instead to let it outspeed Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Greninja after a Shell Smash, at the expense of missing key KOs on physically defensive Corviknight and Garchomp.

Mega Barbaracle should be used on hyper offense and offense teams that can handle the priority users that it can struggle with. Entry hazard leads like Glimmora, Excadrill, and Hisuian Samurott make for great teammates, as they can set hazards to let Mega Barbaracle pick up KOs on threats it otherwise wouldn’t such as against Hippowdon and physically defensive Primarina. Glimmora and Excadrill's access to Mortal Spin and Rapid Spin, respectively, is also appreciated because it can keep hazards off its side of the field, which would otherwise hinder Mega Barbaracle's longevity and sweeping potential. Hazard removal can allow Mega Barbaracle to survive weak attacks despite its Defense drops following a Shell Smash. Hisuian Samurott's access to the combination of Flip Turn and Encore is beneficial, as it can pivot out on locked foes like Corviknight and Kingambit in order to give Mega Barbaracle the opportunity to get a Shell Smash off. Due to Mega Barbaracle's immense vulnerability to priority, particularly from Mega Lopunny's Mach Punch, Scizor and Mega Metagross's Bullet Punch, and Hisuian Samurott's Aqua Jet, it appreciates bulkier setup sweepers like Dragon Dance Dragonite and Calm Mind Primarina that can survive priority attacks and threaten these Pokemon in return. Volcarona is also a great teammate, as it can switch in on Scizor's and Mega Metagross's Bullet Punch while threatening a burn and begin setting up. Mega Barbaracle functions as a great teammate to Swords Dance sweepers like Garchomp, Sneasler, and Scizor, since it can easily take care of Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, which can often trade with these Pokemon. Sneasler and Scizor in particular are great teammates, as Sneasler can threaten Mega Meganium, and both can pressure Unaware Clefable, which ignores Mega Barbaracle's Shell Smash boosts and stops its sweep. On more balanced teams, Corviknight and Galarian Slowking can function as great teammates, as they can bring Mega Barbaracle in safely with their pivoting moves; additionally, Corviknight can remove hazards with Defog, and Galarian Slowking can pressure potential switch-ins to Mega Barbaracle with Future Sight.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Mega Dragalge's unique defensive typing, incredible special bulk, ability Regenerator, and access to Flip Turn make it an excellent defensive pivot. Mega Dragalge uses these traits to check numerous special threats such as Mega Meganium, non-Psychic Volcarona, Mega Raichu Y, and Rotom-Wash and even physical threats such as Sneasler, generating momentum with Flip Turn by forcing switches. Flip Turn also allows Mega Dragalge to take advantage of passive Pokemon, notably underspeeding Corviknight's U-turn. Sludge Bomb lets Mega Dragalge pressure Fairy-types such as Clefable, Primarina, Mega Meganium, and Mega Floette while threatening to poison non-immune foes. Draco Meteor is a powerful STAB option that prevents fellow Dragon-types from coming in freely, such as Garchomp and Dragapult, while also dealing enormous damage to most foes that do not resist it, such as Archaludon, Sneasler, and Rotom-Wash. Scald lets Mega Dragalge threaten burns, discouraging physical threats such as Mega Metagross, Kingambit, and Aegislash from switching in. It can also cripple opposing defensive Pokemon such as Toxapex, Galarian Slowking, and Corviknight with passive chip damage. Toxic is an alternative to Scald, allowing Mega Dragalge to more reliably check Volcarona, Calm Mind Primarina, and Mega Floette by putting them on a timer. Toxic Spikes is an option as well to target teams without an absorber. The SP spread allows Mega Dragalge to survive Garchomp's Earthquake and Mega Delphox's Psyshock while still avoiding the 2HKO from Moonblast by Calm Mind-boosted Primarina or Mega Floette.

Mega Dragalge faces competition from Toxapex and Galarian Slowking, which can similarly function as specially defensive pivots that absorb Toxic Spikes. Therefore, Mega Dragalge best fits on balance teams in search of a defensive pivot that can cover most of the roles filled by the aforementioned Pokemon while reliably handling Mega Raichu Y and Mega Charizard Y, which are otherwise quite difficult to check defensively. Mega Dragalge is threatened by numerous physical threats such as Mega Metagross, Excadrill, and Garchomp, so it should be paired with a strong physical wall, such as Corviknight or Hippowdon, both of which benefit from how Mega Dragalge checks Mega Raichu Y, Mega Meganium, and Rotom-Wash. Powerful wallbreakers that appreciate switch-in opportunities against Steel- and Poison-types, such as Aegislash, Ceruledge, and Garchomp, would complement Mega Dragalge's ability to bring them in safely with Flip Turn. Galarian Slowking is particularly annoying for Mega Dragalge, as none of Mega Dragalge's moves threaten it, allowing Galarian Slowking to set up Future Sight and pivot out with a slower Chilly Reception. Thus, Hisuian Samurott and Meowscarada make great partners with Mega Dragalge, taking advantage of many Pokemon that threaten it like Galarian Slowking, Aegislash, and Mega Delphox while benefiting from how Mega Dragalge checks Fighting- and Fairy-types in return. Mega Dragalge is less reliable at checking certain Fairy-types such as Calm Mind Mega Floette than other Poison-types; therefore, a secondary answer such as Excadrill or Aegislash is appreciated.

IronPress.description:
Iron Defense Corviknight is an excellent defensive Pokemon and wincon. It can boost alongside setup sweepers such as Kingambit, Dragonite, and Garchomp, allowing it to continue checking them while threatening significant damage with Body Press. Corviknight's fantastic typing, resilience to entry hazards, and key resistances grant it many opportunities to set up throughout a game. Corviknight can extend its utility with Defog, given its great matchup against foes like defensive Garchomp and Hippowdon, thanks in part to Pressure. Alternatively, Corviknight can run Brave Bird to hit threats that would otherwise check it, such as Volcarona, Mega Meganium, and Mega Delphox, as well as Ghost-types like Annihilape and Ceruledge, preventing them from switching in. Leftovers is Corviknight's preferred item, with the passive healing over time being crucial for checking hazard setters and limiting how often it needs to use Roost. Sitrus Berry is also a good option if another teammate is already using Leftovers, and has the added benefit of allowing Corviknight to avoid Poltergeist from Pokemon such as Aegislash after it is consumed. Occa Berry allows Corviknight to survive an otherwise lethal Fire-type attack from Pokemon such as Blaziken, Mega Meganium, and Volcarona. Occa Berry pairs especially well with Brave Bird, as Corviknight can lure in Blaziken, Mega Meganium, and Volcarona and potentially KO them in return. 16 Speed SPs can be used to allow Corviknight to outrun maximum Speed Adamant Kingambit and use Iron Defense before Kingambit attacks. However, this requires Corviknight to sacrifice a notable amount of physical bulk, and it already outspeeds bulkier Kingambit variants without the investment. Mental Herb is another option, allowing Corviknight to avoid being locked into a move by Encore from users such as Maushold and Hisuian Samurott. However, because Encore is uncommon, other items are typically more effective.

Corviknight can fit on a wide variety of teams thanks to its ability to clear entry hazards and check a number of dangerous Pokemon such as Garchomp, Sneasler, and Kingambit, though it will find particular success on balance and bulky offense teams. Corviknight benefits greatly from entry hazard support because many of its answers, such as Mega Delphox, Ceruledge, and Mega Raichu Y, lack reliable recovery or are weak to Stealth Rock. Bulky entry hazard setters such as Garchomp and Hippowdon are thus great partners, as they can set up Stealth Rock to wear down Corviknight's key checks while also handling certain Fire-types such as Blaziken and Ceruledge and switching into Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon. Corviknight also fits well on hazard-centric teams because Pressure punishes Defog from opposing Corviknight, and Corviknight itself is a great counter to Rapid Spin Excadrill. Key Regenerator Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking, Mega Dragalge, and Toxapex greatly appreciate Corviknight's ability to handle physical attackers such as Kingambit and Garchomp as well as remove entry hazards with Defog. In turn, they can handle special attackers that threaten Corviknight, such as Mega Meganium, Mega Charizard Y, Primarina, and Mega Raichu Y. With or without Brave Bird, Corviknight can find itself struggling against Ghost-types such as Annihilape, Ceruledge, Dragapult, and Aegislash. Hisuian Samurott is a fantastic partner, as it can switch into many of these Ghost-types as well as Fire-type attacks aimed at Corviknight and capitalize on this to begin setting up entry hazards with Ceaseless Edge. It can also revenge kill key threats such as Mega Delphox and Mega Raichu Y either with a Choice Scarf set or by using Sucker Punch. Hydreigon can similarly switch into many of these Pokemon and revenge kill them with Dark Pulse on a Choice Scarf set. However, both Pokemon struggle against Annihilape, so another partner to handle it, such as Clefable or Mega Meganium, is recommended.

Hex.description: Hex Dragapult works well on offense teams, with its Ghost typing preventing entry hazard removal from Rapid Spin users such as Excadrill. Dragapult's high Speed alongside Clear Body makes it a crucial asset against Sticky Web Araquanid. Alternatively, Infiltrator allows Hex Dragapult to cripple Pokemon with Will-O-Wisp behind Substitute such as Bulk Up Annihilape and Dragonite with status, racking passive damage to bring them into revenge killing range. Hisuian Samurott is one of its best partners, setting Spikes with Ceaseless Edge, while Garchomp and Glimmora can set Stealth Rock; these hazards chip down switch-ins to the range of an OHKO by Hex, with Glimmora being able to set Toxic Spikes, allowing Hex to receive a doubled power boost immediately. Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott, Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Kingambit can threaten to revenge kill Dragapult, making Fairy-types such as Mega Meganium good partners. Mega Meganium threatens to deal significant damage with Dazzling Gleam, resists Dark- and Dragon-type attacks thrown at Dragapult, and has Weather Ball to OHKO Kingambit. Ghost-types such as Ceruledge pair nicely as offensive partners to chip down Dark-type Pokemon trying to switch in, whereas Mega Lopunny serves as a physical attacker that handles Kingambit while appreciating Dragapult dealing with Corviknight and Galarian Slowking. Dragapult being able to burn Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott assists Psychic-types such as Mega Delphox and Mega Metagross. Will-O-Wisp can cripple defensive Pokemon such as Corviknight, opening up Dragapult's teammates such as Swords Dance Garchomp and Blaziken to sweep while boosting the power of Hex against Pokemon such as Primarina, Galarian Slowking, and Toxapex. Burn's physical damage reduction also allows Dragapult to soft check Pokemon such as Mega Staraptor and Mega Swampert, and its multitude of resistances help spread paralysis to prevent a sweep against Pokemon such as Swords Dance Blaziken and Quaquaval. Hex Dragapult also works well on bulky balance teams as their main speed control and progress maker, soft checking threatening Pokemon such as Mega Raichu Y while bulky partners such as Clefable and Umbreon can sponge Dark-type attacks as well as threaten with status moves such as Thunder Wave and Toxic.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Dragapult provides amazing speed control by outspeeding Choice Scarf Meowscarada and even +2 Blaziken while also providing good damage output with its Ghost and Dragon-type STAB moves, allowing it to clean late-game. Choice Scarf allows Dragapult to gain a higher Speed tier to revenge kill boosted sweepers while remaining an effective spinblocker and a fast pivot with U-turn. Shadow Ball is its spammable STAB option, while Draco Meteor provides a one-time nuke, stopping sweepers such as Swords Dance Garchomp and Blaziken. U-turn allows Dragapult to maintain momentum by pivoting while also chipping down switch-ins such as Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Primarina. Dragapult also outspeeds Meowscarada and OHKOes it. Flamethrower allows Dragapult to chip Pokemon such as Kingambit and Excadrill and deal massive damage against Corviknight and Scizor.
